validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION confirmed independently of GEM: FERC docket CP20-8-000 (Federal Register notice of application, Oct. 28, 2019; FERC's own March 2020 Environmental Assessment CP20-8-EA.pdf) and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical-projects workbook (row: 'Grand Chenier XPress Project' / 'ANR Pipeline', Docket CP20-8, Status=Completed) both independently name this exact project: ANR Pipeline Company's compression/meter-station expansion in Acadia, Jefferson Davis, and Cameron Parishes, LA, adding firm transportation capacity from ANR's Southeast Head station to the Mermentau River GCX Meter Station to feed Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass LNG terminal via the (separate, Venture-Global-owned) TransCameron Pipeline. Correctly classified Gas/transmission (NGA section 7 certificated interstate pipeline). DUPLICATE check: no other row on the 44-PID Gulf-Coast-in-dev roster names ANR, Grand Chenier, Eunice, or Mermentau; not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: Owner/Operator = ANR Pipeline Co, 100%, confirmed by both the FERC filing and TC Energy's 2023 Annual Information Form. TWO SOURCING NOTES: (1) the gem.wiki page's citation 'TC Energy Announces $400 Million ANR Pipeline Enhancement Project' (Pipeline & Gas Journal, Aug. 2020, cite_note-pgj-7) is NOT about Grand Chenier XPress -- read in full, it describes a different, unrelated ANR project (the Elwood Power Project / ANR Horsepower Replacement Project, a Midwest facilities-modernization project serving a power plant, in-service Nov. 2022, $400M) that happens to also be on the ANR system. It was NOT used as a ref for any GCX value here and should not be cited for this segment row. (2) CAPACITY NUANCE (not a material spec conflict): FERC's 2019 application / 2020 EA describe the AS-FILED incremental capacity as 400 MMcf/d (400,000 Dth/d); EIA's completed-project database records the AS-BUILT 'Additional Capacity' as 420 MMcf/d, matching the sheet's recorded 420.00 MMcf/d exactly -- the sheet's value is the as-completed figure and is confirmed, not disputed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's LastUpdated (2025-08-07) is recent, but Status itself is stale by more than four years: the project has been fully in service since January 2022. Evidence trail: FERC certificated the project at its June 18, 2020 meeting (docket CP20-8-000; certificate issuance confirmed via contemporaneous reporting, S&P Global Commodity Insights, though that specific article page 403-blocked automated fetch and is not cited as a ref here); TC Energy brought Phase I online in April 2021 (per S&P Global Commodity Insights reporting on FERC's April 20, 2021 letter order clearing partial service -- same caveat, page blocked, not cited) and Phase II (full project) in January 2022, per TC Energy's own project fact sheet and its 2023 Annual Information Form. Independently, EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical database -- compiled by EIA, not sourced from GEM or TC Energy -- lists this exact project (Docket CP20-8, operator ANR Pipeline) as Status='Completed', Year In Service Date=2022. Two independent origins (TC Energy's own disclosures + EIA's government database) agree: this row should move from 'construction' to 'operating' with StartYear1=2022 (already recorded) and StartMonth1=1 added.
